speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've shared your symptoms, but I need to clarify a few details. Have you noticed any recent changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation, and do you experience any fever?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant amount of weight loss. Have you noticed any night sweats, and has your abdominal pain radiated to your back or shoulder?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: It is possible, but the supraclavicular lymphadenopathy combined with significant weight loss and night sweats also raises concern for lymphoma or malignancy. Given the severity of your symptoms, I need to evaluate your lymph nodes and abdominal organs immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck ultrasound and Abdominal CT. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and LDH.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital_Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood_Pressure 135/80 mmHg, Heart_Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory_Rate 14 breaths/min. Neck_Examination: Nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node observed. Abdominal_Examination: Slight abdominal distension, normal bowel sounds, dullness noted over the left lower quadrant, splenomegaly detected without rebound tenderness. Blood_Work: Complete_Blood_Count shows Elevated WBC, Slightly Decreased Hemoglobin, Normal Platelets; Lactate_Dehydrogenase is Elevated. Imaging: CT_Scan_Thorax_and_Abdomen reveals massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Biopsy: Cervical_Lymph_Node findings show lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), massive lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, elevated LDH, and a CD20-positive biopsy confirms a high-grade B-cell lymphoma.
